source: We collected blood samples from 100 metastatic NSCLC patients before and after ICI for high-depth sequencing of the CHIP panel and 63 samples for blood single-cell RNA sequencing.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the sample collection and sequencing approach in the abstract.

claim: 63 samples were collected for blood single-cell RNA sequencing.
source: We collected blood samples from 100 metastatic NSCLC patients before and after ICI for high-depth sequencing of the CHIP panel and 63 samples for blood single-cell RNA sequencing.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of samples used for scRNA-seq in the abstract.

claim: Whole exome sequencing was performed in an independent replication cohort of 180 patients.
source: Whole exome sequencing was performed in an independent replication cohort of 180 patients.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the replication cohort size and sequencing method in the abstract.

claim: The impact of CHIP status on the immunotherapy response was not significant.
source: The impact of CHIP status on the immunotherapy response was not significant.

claim: Metastatic lung cancer patients showed higher CHIP prevalence compared to controls (44/100 for patients vs. 5/42 for controls; p = 0.01).
source: However, metastatic lung cancer patients showed higher CHIP prevalence (44/100 for patients vs. 5/42 for controls; p = 0.01).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numerical data and statistical significance for CHIP prevalence comparison.

claim: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) patients showed increased burden of larger clones compared to lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) patients (8/43 for LUSC vs. 2/50 for LUAD; p = 0.04).
source: In addition, lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) patients showed increased burden of larger clones compared to lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) patients (8/43 for LUSC vs. 2/50 for LUAD; p = 0.04).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numerical data and statistical significance for the comparison between LUSC and LUAD patients.

claim: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis showed significant enrichment of inflammatory pathways mediated by NF-κB in myeloid clusters of the severe CHIP group.
source: Furthermore, single-cell RNA-seq analysis of the matched patients showed significant enrichment of inflammatory pathways mediated by NF-κB in myeloid clusters of the severe CHIP group.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from scRNA-seq analysis in the abstract.

claim: Somatic mutations detected in hematopoietic malignancies are commonly observed with clonal expansion in individuals with no hematological conditions.
source: Recent studies have revealed that somatic mutations detected in hematopoietic malignancies are also commonly observed with clonal expansion in the individuals with no hematological conditions (Jaiswal et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study to support this claim.

claim: Asymptomatic cases with a variant allele frequency (VAF) of ≥2% are defined as clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP).
source: Among such individuals, asymptomatic cases with a variant allele frequency (VAF) of ≥2% are defined as clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) (Jaiswal and Ebert, 2019).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study to support this definition.

claim: CHIP is strongly associated with aging.
source: In general, CHIP is strongly associated with aging; and mutagenic anticancer therapies and smoking can also induce clonal expansion in specific genes (Jaiswal et al., 2014; Hsu et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this association.

claim: Mutagenic anticancer therapies and smoking can induce clonal expansion in specific genes.
source: In general, CHIP is strongly associated with aging; and mutagenic anticancer therapies and smoking can also induce clonal expansion in specific genes (Jaiswal et al., 2014; Hsu et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) carrying CHIP mutations serve as a major source of expanded clones.
source: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) carrying CHIP mutations serve as a major source of expanded clones, and even a few cells are sufficient to influence clonal homeostasis (Welch et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study to support this claim.

claim: Even a few HSPC cells carrying CHIP mutations are sufficient to influence clonal homeostasis.
source: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) carrying CHIP mutations serve as a major source of expanded clones, and even a few cells are sufficient to influence clonal homeostasis (Welch et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study to support this claim.

claim: DNMT3A, ASXL1, and TET2 are representative CHIP mutation-carrying genes.
source: Representative CHIP mutation-carrying genes, such as DNMT3A, ASXL1, and TET2, impact the myeloid population, including monocytes and granulocytes, and have been linked to hematologic malignancies such as myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia through inflammation mediated by the NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome (Muto et al., 2020; Cai et al., 2018; Abplanalp et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: DNMT3A, ASXL1, and TET2 impact the myeloid population, including monocytes and granulocytes.
source: Representative CHIP mutation-carrying genes, such as DNMT3A, ASXL1, and TET2, impact the myeloid population, including monocytes and granulocytes, and have been linked to hematologic malignancies such as myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia through inflammation mediated by the NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome (Muto et al., 2020; Cai et al., 2018; Abplanalp et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: DNMT3A, ASXL1, and TET2 have been linked to hematologic malignancies such as myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia through inflammation mediated by the NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome.
source: Representative CHIP mutation-carrying genes, such as DNMT3A, ASXL1, and TET2, impact the myeloid population, including monocytes and granulocytes, and have been linked to hematologic malignancies such as myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia through inflammation mediated by the NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome (Muto et al., 2020; Cai et al., 2018; Abplanalp et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: The prevalence of clonal hematopoiesis (CH) in cancer patients is significantly higher than that in healthy populations.
source: The prevalence of clonal hematopoiesis (CH) in cancer patients is also significantly higher than that in healthy populations, and high CH burden has been implicated in a negative effect on overall survival in multiple cancer types (Coombs et al., 2017; Bolton et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: High CH burden has been implicated in a negative effect on overall survival in multiple cancer types.
source: The prevalence of clonal hematopoiesis (CH) in cancer patients is also significantly higher than that in healthy populations, and high CH burden has been implicated in a negative effect on overall survival in multiple cancer types (Coombs et al., 2017; Bolton et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: CHIP is associated with atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
source: CHIP is also associated with diseases beyond hematologic malignancies, such as atherosclerosis, type 2 diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (Miller et al., 2022; Tobias et al., 2023; Jaiswal et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) stands out globally as the solid tumor with the highest mortality burden.
source: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) stands out globally as the solid tumor with the highest mortality burden (Leiter et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study to support this claim.

claim: The difficulty in early detection of NSCLC significantly contributes to its mortality rate being high compared to its incidence rate.
source: The difficulty in early detection of NSCLC significantly contributes to its mortality rate being high compared to its incidence rate.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge about NSCLC.

claim: Recent studies indicate a possible association of lung cancer risk with CH.
source: Recent studies examining CHIP within lung cancer cohorts and general population indicate a possible association of lung cancer risk with CH (Stacey et al., 2023; Hong et al., 2022; Tian et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting PD-(L)1 and CTLA-4 have revolutionized treatment of advanced NSCLC.
source: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting PD-(L)1 and CTLA-4 have revolutionized treatment of advanced NSCLC, both as monotherapies and in combination with chemotherapy (Reck et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study to support this claim.

claim: Response rates to ICI treatments remain relatively low.
source: However, response rates to ICI treatments remain relatively low.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge about ICI treatments.

claim: The predictive ability of markers like PD-1 expression and tumor mutational burden is insufficient.
source: The predictive ability of markers like PD-1 expression and tumor mutational burden is insufficient, requiring the identification of additional markers.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge about current predictive markers.

claim: Recent studies suggest a marginal effect of ICI on the clonal dynamics of CHIP.
source: Recent studies suggest a marginal effect of ICI on the clonal dynamics of CHIP (Miller et al., 2021; Miller et al., 2020), but the current understanding of the role of CHIP in ICI-treated patients is not comprehensive.
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: 67 CHIP mutations were identified in 100 patients at baseline.
source: At the baseline, we identified 67 CHIP mutations in 100 patients, 26 of them in known putative driver genes of hematopoietic cancer (CHIP-PD).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numerical data from their analysis.

claim: 26 CHIP mutations were in known putative driver genes of hematopoietic cancer (CHIP-PD) at baseline.
source: At the baseline, we identified 67 CHIP mutations in 100 patients, 26 of them in known putative driver genes of hematopoietic cancer (CHIP-PD).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numerical data from their analysis.

claim: After treatment, 68 CHIP and 32 CHIP-PD mutations were found in 91 patients who passed quality control assessment.
source: After treatment, 68 CHIP and 32 CHIP-PD mutations were found in 91 patients who passed quality control assessment (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplements 1–3, and Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numerical data from their analysis and references figures.

claim: DNMT3A, PPM1D, and TET2 were the most frequently mutated CHIP genes.
source: Among the CHIP genes, DNMT3A, PPM1D, and TET2 were the most frequently mutated (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references a figure.

claim: PPM1D truncating mutations have previously demonstrated association with patients' smoking habits and possible history with chemotherapy.
source: PPM1D truncating mutations were also common, and have previously demonstrated association with patients' smoking habits and possible history with chemotherapy (Hsu et al., 2018; Coombs et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: ICI treatment effected minimal changes in CHIP burden.
source: Overall, we observed ICI treatment to effect minimal changes in CHIP burden (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references a figure.

claim: VAF was highly correlated across all traced mutations and not dependent on clinical responses.
source: Also, VAF was highly correlated across all traced mutations and not dependent on clinical responses (Figure 1C, D).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references figures.

claim: Increased number of CHIP mutations with VAF >10% was noted in patients with lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC).
source: However, we noted increased number of CHIP mutations with VAF >10% in patients with lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis.

claim: CHIP prevalence was significantly higher in the lung cancer cohort compared to the control group (controls 5/42 vs. patients 44/100, age-adjusted logistic regression p = 0.01).
source: CHIP prevalence was significantly higher in the lung cancer cohort compared to the control group (controls 5/42 vs. patients 44/100, age-adjusted logistic regression p = 0.01; Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1a and b).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numerical data and statistical significance for this comparison.

claim: The number of CHIP-positive patients did not differ before and after ICI treatment.
source: However, the number of CHIP-positive patients did not differ before and after ICI treatment, nor in relation to treatment response (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references figures.

claim: The number of CHIP-positive patients did not differ in relation to treatment response.
source: However, the number of CHIP-positive patients did not differ before and after ICI treatment, nor in relation to treatment response (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references figures.

claim: CHIP burden is heavily dependent on age.
source: As previously reported, CHIP burden is heavily dependent on age (Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript references previous reports and their own data shown in a figure.

claim: High CHIP burden was prevalent in LUSC.
source: Taking CHIP VAF as an indicator of clonal size, we observed that high CHIP burden was prevalent in LUSC, while multiple concurrent CHIP mutations were common in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) patients (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references figures.

claim: Multiple concurrent CHIP mutations were common in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) patients.
source: Taking CHIP VAF as an indicator of clonal size, we observed that high CHIP burden was prevalent in LUSC, while multiple concurrent CHIP mutations were common in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) patients (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references figures.

claim: 468,596 cells were retrieved in a total of 26 clusters from PBMC scRNA-seq data.
source: After quality control processes, we retrieved 468,596 cells in a total of 26 clusters defined by systemic integration and clustering using the Louvain algorithm, then validated using Azimuth (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B, Supplementary file 1e, and Methods) (Hao et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numerical data from their scRNA-seq analysis and references figures.

claim: Cell composition analysis showed an increased proportion of natural killer (NK) cells after ICI administration.
source: Cell composition analysis showed an increased proportion of natural killer (NK) cells and a decreased CD4 TEM population after ICI administration, but high variability between samples precluded systematic differences by CHIP status (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references a figure.

claim: Cell composition analysis showed a decreased CD4 TEM population after ICI administration.
source: Cell composition analysis showed an increased proportion of natural killer (NK) cells and a decreased CD4 TEM population after ICI administration, but high variability between samples precluded systematic differences by CHIP status (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references a figure.

claim: High variability between samples precluded systematic differences by CHIP status in cell composition.
source: Cell composition analysis showed an increased proportion of natural killer (NK) cells and a decreased CD4 TEM population after ICI administration, but high variability between samples precluded systematic differences by CHIP status (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references a figure.

claim: Gene set enrichment test indicated activation of the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling pathway via NFKB in the high CH burden group for most cell lineages.
source: The results indicated activation of the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling pathway via NFKB in the high CH burden group for most cell lineages, including both classical dendritic cells (DCs) and NK cells (Figure 3D, E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3, and Supplementary file 1g; see Methods).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their gene set enrichment analysis and references figures.

claim: The interactions between ICI treatment response and CHIP burden mostly depended on CH status only, and not on response to ICI.
source: However, the interactions mostly depended on CH status only, and not on response to ICI.
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis.

claim: The 'black module' from WGCNA exhibited myeloid specificity and represented most of the signaling-related DEGs identified via gene set enrichment analysis.
source: First, we used hdWGCNA to construct co-expression networks for genes in myeloid cells, which yielded a black module that exhibited myeloid specificity and represented most of the signaling-related DEGs identified via gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) (Figure 3—figure supplement 5 and Supplementary file 1h; Morabito et al., 2023).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their WGCNA analysis and references a figure.

claim: Gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis using SCENIC indicated that the regulatory activity of transcription factors in the AP-1 and NF-κB pathways was particularly notable in the myeloid lineage of high-burden patients.
source: In addition to weighted correlation network analysis (WGCNA), gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis using SCENIC (Van de Sande et al., 2020; Figure 3—figure supplement 6) indicated that the regulatory activity of transcription factors in the AP-1 and NF-κB pathways was particularly notable in the myeloid lineage of high-burden patients (Figure 3—figure supplement 6A, B).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their GRN analysis and references figures.

claim: Both the NF-κB regulon and the ATF3 regulon were activated in the myeloid cluster of high-burden patients.
source: Both the NF-κB regulon and the ATF3 regulon, which represents the AP-1 pathway, were activated in the myeloid cluster of high-burden patients (Figure 3—figure supplement 6C–E).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their GRN analysis and references figures.

claim: Expansion of HSPC-derived monocytes is the cause of CHIP.
source: Recent studies have shown that expansion of HSPC-derived monocytes is the cause of CHIP, and representative CHIP genes, including DNMT3A and TET2, exert immune-regulatory effects through the NLRP3 inflammasome (Welch et al., 2012; Abplanalp et al., 2021; Sano et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: Representative CHIP genes, including DNMT3A and TET2, exert immune-regulatory effects through the NLRP3 inflammasome.
source: Recent studies have shown that expansion of HSPC-derived monocytes is the cause of CHIP, and representative CHIP genes, including DNMT3A and TET2, exert immune-regulatory effects through the NLRP3 inflammasome (Welch et al., 2012; Abplanalp et al., 2021; Sano et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: A VAF of 10% in heterozygote mutations corresponds to approximately 20% of cells.
source: Notably, a VAF of 10% in heterozygote mutations corresponds to approximately 20% of cells; thus, the presence of such mutations in HSPC-derived monocytes of high-burden patients would have resulted in an overall transcriptional profile change for blood monocytes.
evidence: The manuscript provides this calculation based on genetic principles.

claim: Monocytes and DCs in high-burden cases were activated as receptors for TNF and Lymphotoxin A.
source: However, when the interactions in the TNF and IL-1B pathways were analyzed separately, monocytes and DCs in high-burden cases were activated as receptors for TNF and Lymphotoxin A (Figure 3—figure supplement 7C).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their cell-cell interaction analysis and references a figure.

claim: The progression-free survival (PFS) of patients after ICI treatment was reduced in the high-burden CHIP group (825 vs. 404, p = 0.056).
source: Our results showed the progression-free survival (PFS) of patients after ICI treatment to be reduced in the high-burden CHIP group (825 vs. 404, p = 0.056), with no difference in ICI response rates between the negative and high-burden CHIP groups.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific numerical data and statistical significance for this survival analysis.

claim: There was no difference in ICI response rates between the negative and high-burden CHIP groups.
source: Our results showed the progression-free survival (PFS) of patients after ICI treatment to be reduced in the high-burden CHIP group (825 vs. 404, p = 0.056), with no difference in ICI response rates between the negative and high-burden CHIP groups.
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis.

claim: Previous studies have observed a negative effect on life expectancy in CHIP patients with solid tumors.
source: Previous studies have already observed a negative effect on life expectancy in CHIP patients with solid tumors.
evidence: The manuscript references previous studies to support this claim.

claim: CH prevalence was significantly higher in NSCLC patients.
source: Here, we report that CH prevalence was significantly higher in NSCLC patients and higher burden of mutations with VAF of greater than 10% was frequently observed in LUSC.
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis.

claim: Higher burden of mutations with VAF of greater than 10% was frequently observed in LUSC.
source: Here, we report that CH prevalence was significantly higher in NSCLC patients and higher burden of mutations with VAF of greater than 10% was frequently observed in LUSC.
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis.

claim: Myeloid cells in NSCLC patients with high CH burden exhibit an altered inflammatory milieu via increased NF-κB pathway expression.
source: Using scRNA-seq analysis, we found myeloid cells in NSCLC patients with high CH burden to exhibit an altered inflammatory milieu via increased NF-κB pathway expression.
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: A study linking COVID-19 and CH showed an increased inflammatory response from monocytes in severe COVID-19 patients with CH, mediated via interferon gamma (IFN-γ) and TNF-α signaling signatures.
source: In particular, a study linking COVID-19 and CH showed an increased inflammatory response from monocytes in severe COVID-19 patients with CH, mediated via interferon gamma (IFN-γ) and TNF-α signaling signatures (Choi et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study to support this claim.

claim: Myeloid cells from NSCLC patients with CH tend to harbor increased inflammatory response mediated by NF-κB pathway signaling.
source: Likewise, we observed that myeloid cells from NSCLC patients with CH tend to harbor increased inflammatory response, and this response is mediated by NF-κB pathway signaling (Figure 3).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their data analysis and references a figure.

claim: GSEA results indicated the enrichment of TNF signaling and hypoxia pathways in most clusters of patients with severe CH.
source: Our GSEA results specifically indicated the enrichment of TNF signaling and hypoxia pathways in most clusters of patients with severe CH (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their GSEA analysis and references a figure.

claim: Core genes such as FOS, DUSP1, JUN, and PPP1R15A were shared between the TNF signaling and hypoxia pathways in all significant clusters.
source: The leading edge genes from GSEA results showed core genes such as FOS, DUSP1, JUN, and PPP1R15A, which are known to play critical roles in the inflammatory phenotypes of immune cells, were shared between the TNF signaling and hypoxia pathways in all significant clusters (Figure 3—figure supplement 9).
evidence: The manuscript provides this finding from their GSEA analysis and references a figure.

claim: FOS, DUSP1, JUN, and PPP1R15A are known to play critical roles in the inflammatory phenotypes of immune cells.
source: The leading edge genes from GSEA results showed core genes such as FOS, DUSP1, JUN, and PPP1R15A, which are known to play critical roles in the inflammatory phenotypes of immune cells, were shared between the TNF signaling and hypoxia pathways in all significant clusters (Figure 3—figure supplement 9).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge about these genes.

claim: ICIs modulate pathways involved in immune response rather than cell proliferation.
source: As ICIs modulate pathways involved in immune response rather than cell proliferation, it is reasonable that ICIs do not exert a direct influence on CH development (Miller et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study and provides reasoning based on the mechanism of ICIs.

claim: ICIs do not exert a direct influence on CH development.
source: As ICIs modulate pathways involved in immune response rather than cell proliferation, it is reasonable that ICIs do not exert a direct influence on CH development (Miller et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study to support this claim.

claim: Elevated inflammatory activity in the bloodstream may impact long-term patient survival pre- and post-ICI administration.
source: However, our findings do suggest that elevated inflammatory activity in the bloodstream may impact long-term patient survival pre- and post-ICI administration (Figure 3—figure supplement 8).
evidence: The manuscript provides this interpretation based on their data analysis and references a figure.

claim: Involvement of the IL-1 pathway in the aggressiveness and metastasis of lung cancer has been reported in experimental studies.
source: Notably, involvement of the IL-1 pathway in the aggressiveness and metastasis of lung cancer has been reported in experimental studies (Li et al., 2020; Zhang and Veeramachaneni, 2022), and inhibition of IL-1β has proven effective in reducing lung cancer-related mortality, as shown in the CANTOS trial (Ridker et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous studies to support this claim.

claim: Inhibition of IL-1β has proven effective in reducing lung cancer-related mortality, as shown in the CANTOS trial.
source: Notably, involvement of the IL-1 pathway in the aggressiveness and metastasis of lung cancer has been reported in experimental studies (Li et al., 2020; Zhang and Veeramachaneni, 2022), and inhibition of IL-1β has proven effective in reducing lung cancer-related mortality, as shown in the CANTOS trial (Ridker et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study to support this claim.

claim: More potent factors, such as smoking and anticancer therapies, may have a more substantial impact than immunotherapy on CH.
source: Indeed, it is worth noting that more potent factors, such as smoking and anticancer therapies, may have a more substantial impact than immunotherapy (Bolton et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study to support this claim.

evidence: The manuscript provides specific numerical data comparing their cohort to controls.

claim: The cohort had a higher proportion of males compared to control patients (male/female: 91/9 vs. 18/24).

evidence: The manuscript provides specific numerical data comparing their cohort to controls.

claim: The most prevalent CH mutations, including DNMT3A, TET2, and PPM1D, were marginally affected by smoking.
